page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.8xlarge is a dedicated x86_64 instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor offering 16 physical cores and 32 virtual CPUs with Hyper-Threading enabled. The CPU feature set includes AVX-512 instructions with VNNI support, AES cryptography, and 35 MB of L3 cache. System memory totals 128.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. This instance has no local SSD storage attached and relies on network storage, supported by a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

In synthetic and application benchmarks, the instance demonstrates solid performance across single-core and multi-core workloads. PassMark CPU testing yields a score of 29,517.51, complemented by a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,107.0. Memory bandwidth tests record up to 1,705.41 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 109.89 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. On data processing workloads, the server reaches 28.91 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 21.45 GB/sec. Small 135M model LLM prompt processing achieves 1,539.55 tokens per second, though medium 7B models drop to 45.98 tokens per second due to CPU-only execution without GPU acceleration.

The instance provides cost-effective resource density for compute-intensive enterprise applications that do not require dedicated hardware accelerators or attached local NVMe storage. With 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU and robust vector instruction support, it is well suited for web serving, database operations, software compilation, medium-scale data processing, and general-purpose backend services.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.8xlarge is a general-purpose compute instance equipped with 32 vCPUs and 128.0 GB of RAM, powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor built on the x86_64 architecture and KVM hypervisor. Featuring 16 physical cores with Hyper-Threading, 35 MB of L3 cache, and AVX-512 extensions including VNNI, this instance provides steady multi-core execution for broad application requirements. It features 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without integrated local disk storage. Benchmark evaluations show multi-threaded performance with a PassMark CPU score of 29,517.51, Redis SET handling at 28.91 million operations per second, and web serving throughput reaching 21.45 GB/sec. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 109.89 GB/sec. The balanced 1:4 core-to-memory allocation makes it efficient for software compilation, static web serving, enterprise backend services, and database workloads relying on external network storage.
